Listen to the pain in his voice. The endless suffering of Palestinians in Gaza. ENOUGH IS ENOUGH! Thousands of tents broke overnight, and this young boy in Zaytoun neighborhood is one of them. The Sameer Project is getting hundreds of calls and messages asking for support, and we don’t have the funds to do it! The military occupation closed the Egyptian borders a few days ago, and there are no tents or tarps coming in. War profiteers supported by the military occupation are hoarding tents and tarps, and hiking the prices making it impossible for anyone to afford them. Our choices are to feel hopeless and angry, or mobilize and help as much as we can. The Sameer Project chooses the latter but we NEED your urgent help. Donate urgently to the General Fund and share the crisis in Gaza with everyone you know.

It’s been nine months since I left Gaza. People often think that once you make it out, the suffering ends. It doesn’t. Some days, it feels like it never left. We’re still living with the consequences of that dark day!October 7. The grief didn’t stay behind in Gaza. It followed us. This morning, I lost another one of my cats. She was hit by a car right in front of my home. She’s the eighth out of my nine cats that I’ve lost. Sometimes it feels like life just keeps finding new ways to break what’s left of my heart.. #rip #rest #loss #🐾

Hundreds of Palestinians gathered in Gaza City to celebrate a mass wedding for 250 couples, bringing a moment of happiness to a community still grappling with the devastation of war. Brides wore traditional embroidered Palestinian dresses, while grooms donned keffiyehs as families celebrated marriages that many couples had postponed because of the war and financial hardship. The celebration comes as Palestinians in Gaza continue to face deadly Israeli attacks despite a ceasefire agreement reached in October 2025, with at least 1,600 Palestinians killed since it took effect, according to Gaza's Health Ministry.

Heavy rains have flooded thousands of tents in Gaza, leaving displaced Palestinians struggling to cope with the first winter storm. Meanwhile, Israeli settlers have seized Palestinian homes in Jericho, and Israeli forces have carried out a destructive raid on a Bedouin village in the occupied West Bank.   Al Jazeera’s Nour Hegazy has the latest.
